questions.stem: A dispatcher's log evaluates whether foreign threats alone caused the Red Scare.

answer.exemplar: Domestic political and economic anxieties, not just foreign threats, drove the second Red Scare.

questions.explanation: Domestic factors mattered alongside foreign threats. The log frames internal roots.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY

stimulus.body: The log warns that defense spending created entrenched interests resisting cuts.

questions.stem: A dispatcher's log asks about the military-industrial complex's political effect.

options.text: Spending benefited only foreign contractors.
Defense interests favored deep cuts to military spending.
The complex had no political influence.
Defense interests became entrenched and resisted budget cuts.

questions.explanation: The log frames entrenched interests resisting cuts. Pro-cut and no influence are contradicted.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.stem: A dispatcher's log evaluates whether defense research justified its costs through civilian gains.

options.text: Defense research produced no civilian gains at all.
Civilian gains from defense research were real but uneven and costly.
Costs were negligible and gains universal.
Only the military ever benefited.

questions.explanation: The log balances real but uneven gains against costs. No gains and universal gains are contradicted.
